# hands/film

Teeny's story films, narrated and built audio first.

## How to call it

Run it from the repository root with your shell (exec) tool: `hands/film <verb> [flags]`.

- A verb that takes a body reads one JSON object from stdin. Everything else is flags.
- It prints one JSON object on stdout. Exit 0 is success. Exit 2 is a refusal by a rule, the guard or a cap: read the `rule` and `reason`, and do not retry it unchanged. Any other exit is an error.
- Secrets belong to the hand; you never see them and never pass one.
- The hand runs the guard, its caps and `DRY_RUN` itself. `DRY_RUN` is on unless the box turned it off; under it an acting verb checks every rule and sends nothing. Do not try to go around the hand, and do not look for another way to do what it refused.

## Side effects

docs/hands.md does not mark this hand's verbs as read, acting, job or operator. Treat every verb as acting unless the table below or `hands/film --help` says it only reads.

## Verbs

docs/hands.md has no verb table for this hand.

Verbs named in the hand's source: `due`, `make`.

For one verb's exact flags, run `hands/film <verb> --help` (never put a VAR= in front of a command: the shell refuses it, and DRY_RUN is not yours to set). The full account is in docs/hands.md.
